title: E7 evidence-chain checkpoint form A
instructions: Develop a body paragraph from these original practice notes: Before a school assembly, one mixed queue at two doors caused uncertainty. A student team trialled blue cards for the left door and gold cards for the right door, while one helper redirected anyone in the wrong line. Use only the stated evidence.

parts.prompt: Which topic sentence gives the paragraph the clearest evidence-bearing promise?

options.text: Assemblies are common events in many schools.
The colour-card trial made each entrance choice visible before pupils reached the doors.
The cards were blue and gold, which are attractive colours.
Every queue problem can be solved immediately.

choice_rationales.A: This broad fact gives the paragraph no specific claim to develop.
choice_rationales.B: This names the method and the bounded improvement that the evidence can support.
choice_rationales.C: Colour preference is not the organisational effect of the trial.
choice_rationales.D: The absolute claim goes far beyond one assembly trial.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The paragraph can demonstrate how a visible entrance signal reduced uncertainty without claiming universal success.

parts.prompt: Which TWO details form the strongest action-and-observation pair?

options.text: The team handed each pupil a card matching one of the two doors.
Several pupils checked their cards before joining a line.
The assembly stage curtains were dark red.
The school badge contains three shapes.
Exactly 96.4 per cent of pupils felt calmer, although nobody was surveyed.

choice_rationales.A: This states the concrete method used in the trial.
choice_rationales.B: This observable response shows how the method influenced a decision.
choice_rationales.C: The curtain colour has no role in the queue process.
choice_rationales.D: The badge detail is specific but irrelevant.
choice_rationales.E: The percentage invents evidence that the notes do not contain.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Together, the distributed cards and pupils checking them create a relevant evidence chain from action to response.

parts.prompt: Which explanation best completes the evidence chain?

options.text: This mattered because the choice was made before the bottleneck, leaving the helper to correct exceptions instead of directing every pupil.
This was useful because useful systems are always helpful.
Blue is often associated with calmness in advertisements.
The cards guaranteed that no future assembly would ever have a queue.

choice_rationales.A: This interprets how the method changed the point at which most decisions were made.
choice_rationales.B: This repeats a positive label without explaining the consequence.
choice_rationales.C: Colour symbolism is not evidence from the trial.
choice_rationales.D: One bounded trial cannot guarantee every future result.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The explanation connects the observed behaviour to a specific organisational benefit while respecting the evidence boundary.
